intended_object: Take normal subgroups S ≤ T of a group G and a G-representation A over a commutative ring R. The object is the canonical natural map (A^S)^{T/S} → A^T of G/T-representations, natural in A, where (G/S)/(T/S) is identified with G/T by the third isomorphism theorem. The map is in fact an isomorphism. This is read off the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The two functors are the right ones. The source sends A to the T/S-invariants of the S-invariants of A, which is a (G/S)/(T/S)-representation. The target sends A to A^T, a G/T-representation, and then restricts it along the third-isomorphism equivalence (G/S)/(T/S) ≃ G/T. So both are functors from Rep R G to Rep R ((G/S)/(T/S)).

The component at A is the forward map of `nestedQuotientInvariantsRepIso`. That map is the identity on elements: an element of (A^S)^{T/S} is an element of A fixed by S and by T/S, hence by T. It is equivariant, which is checked in that iso's definition. Naturality comes from a separate lemma that is proved by `rfl`. This is exactly the standard identification (A^S)^{T/S} = A^T.

The generality is the natural one: any group G, any commutative ring R, and any normal subgroups S ≤ T, with no extra hypotheses. Normality of S and T is needed so that the quotient groups and the quotient actions make sense. A grep of Mathlib's RepresentationTheory directory finds no use of `quotientQuotientEquivQuotient`, so this comparison does not appear to be in Mathlib already.

The definition gives the natural transformation rather than a natural isomorphism, although it is invertible. This matches its docstring and is not an error.
